tables.heading: Minor Concepts
representative_rows: width="65%" |Reason And/Or How It Should Happen
Twin able to upgrade into Gunner
Since the Gunner has 4 cannons and the Twin has 2, it should be normal for the Twin to upgrade into Gunner. The Gunner's cannons also fires alternately, like the Twin.

The size of the arena in Sandbox with only one player is too small, a full level Ranger's FoV can show the visual map border on all sides. There should be two keys that can change the arena size, but only the host of the server should be able to do that.

The walls in Maze aren't arranged well (to be honest) which may form large compact walls that only takes large mass of space, making the game much harder for players that newly joined the server. If this happens in the Pentagon Nest, then either the Pentagons are all stuck in the middle of the wall, or it may just prevent spawning of them, thus "removing" the nest itself; perhaps the swarm of Crashers are still there.
Fairer FFA (and the like) mechanics and gameplay

Seriously, players who newly spawned are often being killed by the ones who managed to survive and became Level 45 tanks. Usually, the leaderboard shows that less than 10 (or even 4) players are Level 45 (or Tier 4) tanks, with their score notably higher than the next ones.
tables.raw_wikitext: {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" style="width: 100%" ! width="35%" |Game-Changing Concept ! width="65%" |Reason And/Or How It Should Happen |- |Twin able to upgrade into Gunner |Since the Gunner has 4 cannons and the Twin has 2, it should be normal for the Twin to upgrade into Gunner. The Gunner's cannons also fires alternately, like the Twin. |- |Changeable arena size in Sandbox |The size of the arena in Sandbox with only one player is too small, a full level Ranger's FoV can show the visual map border on all sides. There should be two keys that can change the arena size, but only the host of the server should be able to do that. |- |Better wall placement in Maze |The walls in Maze aren't arranged well (to be honest) which may form large compact walls that only takes large mass of space, making the game much harder for players that newly joined the server. If this happens in the Pentagon Nest, then either the Pentagons are all stuck in the middle of the wall, or it may just prevent spawning of them, thus "removing" the nest itself; perhaps the swarm of Crashers are still there. |- |Fairer FFA (and the like) mechanics and gameplay |Seriously, players who newly spawned are often being killed by the ones who managed to survive and became Level 45 tanks. Usually, the leaderboard shows that less than 10 (or even 4) players are Level 45 (or Tier 4) tanks, with their score notably higher than the next ones. |- | Bringing Mothership game mode back |The game mode has been popular during its lifetime. Removing it for Maze is not a good way to implement wall features. Perhaps making new servers for Maze is better, with Mothership servers still running for good sake. This is especially jarring after Survival was introduced without any other game mode replaced. |- |Rework of Auto Smasher in terms of stats |Currently, the Auto Smasher is one of the least used tanks in the game. Not because of being added secretly without any mentioned changelog, but because of its lack of stat points to accommodate its massive upgradable stats. Allowing to upgrade a stat 10 times each, but you only have 33 stats points to use is a major problem here (33/80 filled, compared to most other tanks, 33/56 filled). It might be a good idea to make the bullet stats depends on Body Damage, instead of having individual stat to upgrade on. Of course, the auto turret should still be weaker than Auto Gunner's and Auto Trapper's auto turrets, but still decent enough to deal noticeable damage against opponents. |- |Ability to play as Special Tanks in Sandbox again |As of a recent unmentioned update, Mothership, Arena Closer and all three types of Dominators are no longer available to be played as in Sandbox mode, even by using \ key. This is such a bad move that limits the fun value of Sandbox mode, which is its main purpose. As such, the change should be reverted back. |}

tables.heading: Tank Upgrades
representative_rows:
[[Twin]]
Choosing the Twin class grants an extra frontal Cannon while bullet power is slightly reduced. The high rate of fire increases the recoil.

[[Sniper]]
Choosing the Sniper Class grants a broader field of view allowing the player to see further. Bullet Speed is also increased, increasing the bullet's distance. However, Reload speed decreases noticeably. Damage is not increased.

[[Machine Gun]]
The Machine Gun sprays its Bullets from a trapezoid on the front. It fires double the rate of a basic tank, the same rate of the Twin. It is less accurate but it covers a wider area. Bullet damage is slightly higher than the twin but less than the basic.

[[Flank Guard]]
Choosing the Flank Guard class adds a Cannon on the rear. This allows the player to shoot in both directions to defend their back. Because both Cannons have identical Recoil, the Flank Guard effectively has no recoil.

tables.heading: Twin Upgrades
representative_rows:
colspan="2" |[[Triple Shot]]
Choosing the Triple Shot class adds another Cannon and spreads the guns across the front. Triple Shot can cover a wide area with Bullets, but direct firepower is significantly decreased. Recoil will propel the player backward.

colspan="2" |[[Quad Tank]]
The Quad Tank has four guns spread over its sides like a plus sign allowing the player to fire Bullets in 4 directions. Direct firepower is significantly less than before. Recoil is nullified. Also upgrades from the Flank Guard.

colspan="2" |[[Twin Flank]]
The Twin Flank mirrors the Twin’s guns to the rear, adding an extra defense to the back. Recoil also nullified. Also upgrades from the Flank Guard.

tables.heading: Sniper Upgrades
representative_rows:
colspan="3" | [[Assassin]]
Choosing the Assassin class further improves upon the Sniper’s vision. The Field of view increases at the cost of slower Reload speed.

colspan="3" |[[Overseer]]
The Overseer has Spawners that generate [[Drones]] instead of shooting Bullets. Holding the left mouse button, holding "Space", or pressing “E” causes the Drones to follow the player's cursor, while the right mouse button or "Shift" sends all Drones away from the cursor's current location, allowing for manual control. Otherwise, the Drones surround the player and fly out to attack nearby Polygons. Overseers have a maximum of eight Drones.

colspan="3" |[[Hunter]]
The Hunter houses a smaller gun inside of its main Cannon and fires in a two-round burst. The field of view increases slightly.

colspan="3" |[[Trapper]]
The Trapper replaces the Sniper’s Cannon with a [[Launcher]] that fires [[Traps]] that have tremendous penetration. A Launcher’s range is much shorter than a Cannon’s range as the traps completely stop moving after a second. This creates a protective wall that can stop enemy bullets or block an area. it is advised to stay as a sniper or the basic until level 45 due to the difficulty of farming as the Trapper.

tables.heading: Machine Gun Upgrades
representative_rows:
[[Destroyer]]
The Destroyer features a massive, slow-firing Cannon that delivers a single giant Bullet with each shot. Firing the Cannon creates a high amount of recoil. With enough points in Bullet stats, it can penetrate a wall of bullets and still have enough power to one-shot a tank. The Destroyer branch has the strongest level 45 ammunition in the game. The bullet is close to 6 times stronger than most medium-sized bullets and is difficult to stop.

[[Gunner]]
The Gunner rapidly fires small Bullets in a straight path from four frontal miniguns. Reload speed doubles at the cost of decreased damage. Recoil is reduced significantly. The small bullets can bypass enemy defenses and chip away at their health.

'''[[Shotgun]]'''
The Shotgun fires 12 bullets at a high speed that slowly spread out as they travel. Each individual bullet is fairly weak on its own, but the clump of them can deal significant damage. Recoil is increased.

tables.heading: Flank Guard Upgrades
representative_rows:
colspan="3" |[[Tri-Angle]]
The Tri-Angle features two rear Cannons positioned to provide additional thrust when fired. The Tri-Angle can propel itself with recoil while shooting from the front. The rear bullets are about four to five times weaker than the front cannon bullets, making them one of the weakest bullets in the game and giving them a very poor bullet size to damage ratio.

colspan="3" |[[Quad Tank]]
The Quad Tank has four guns spread over its sides, allowing the player to fire Bullets in all directions. Direct firepower is significantly less than before. Recoil is disabled. Also upgrades from the Twin.

colspan="3" |[[Twin Flank]]
The Twin Flank adds an extra Cannon in the front and the rear to the Flank Guard. Recoil is disabled. Also upgrades from the Twin.

colspan="3" |[[Auto 3]]
The Auto 3 features three [[Auto Turrets]] mounted on the side. The tank constantly rotates slowly while its turrets automatically track and fire at the closest entities. The turrets can be manually controlled to an extent; holding down the left mouse button will target the cursor with one or two turrets based on their position. Holding down the right mouse button will make the turrets face away from the cursor.

tables.heading: Tank Upgrades
representative_rows:
[[Smasher]]
The Smasher is a dedicated ramming tank. Choosing the Smasher removes cannons and all Bullet upgrade options and allows the tank to hold ten upgrades in each body upgrade slot instead of seven. The field of view also increases to sniper level. Any points put into bullets are refunded for use in the now available slots upon upgrading. The only available slots in order from the top down are Max Health, Health Regen, Body Damage, and Movement Speed.

tables.heading: Triple Shot Upgrades
representative_rows:
colspan="2" |[[Triplet]]
The Triplet has an extra Cannon compared to the Twin, which significantly increases its firing rate, and it is one of the fastest shooters in the game. It is recommended for a level 30 Twin to avoid upgrading to Triple Shot until getting to level 45, as a Triple Shot's Bullets are very spread out and have little direct firepower. The triplets' bullets are actually slightly weaker than a twins' bullets to balance out the tanks' high firepower.

colspan="2" |[[Penta Shot]]
The Penta Shot can fire 5 Bullets at a rapid speed. It will shoot the whole area in front of the tank with a barrage of Bullets, similarly to the Octo Tank, although the guns are much closer together and only shoots in front of the tank. It has very high recoil.

colspan="2" |[[Spread Shot]]
A class with eleven Cannons! The Spread Shot shoots these simultaneously and, as its name implies, generates a massive “spread” of Bullets which have surprisingly high Penetration. The center Cannon fires a normal-sized Bullet (similar to the basic tanks' bullet), while the other ten Cannons fire gunner bullets. It has almost no recoil.

tables.heading: Quad Tank Upgrades
representative_rows:
[[Octo Tank]]
The Octo Tank allows the player to shoot in 8 directions, with each Cannon being equidistantly spaced from the others. This results in a storm of Bullets that spread throughout the area. The cannons shoot in an alternating pattern of four opposite cannons in a cross shape at once then the other four. The player can press C to turn on auto spin for even bullet distribution all around.

[[Auto 5]]
The Auto 5 upgrades from the Quad Tank getting one more gun and replacing all Cannons with Auto Turrets. The player can control 2-3 Turrets and have more firepower. The Turrets can’t rotate as much, though. Also upgrades from the Auto 3.

representative_rows:
[[Triple Twin]]
The Triple Twin allows the player to have three sets of Twin Cannons, each set spaced at an equal distance away from the others. This will spread the Bullets in a fashion similar to the Octo Tank. Although it is not as spread out, the direct firepower is significantly greater.

[[Battleship]]
The Battleship replaces all of the player's Cannons with Mini Spawners that pump out Drones at an extremely fast rate. Half the drones are manually controlled, and half are auto-controlled. However, Drones automatically disappear 4 seconds after spawning. These drones are also known as Partisans. Also upgrades from the Overseer.

tables.heading: Assassin Upgrades
representative_rows:
[[Ranger]]
The Ranger is exactly like the Assassin, except that its Field of View is larger than those of the Assassin and the Stalker. It has the highest vision range of any tank and requires great skill to land shots from afar.

[[Stalker]]
The Stalker has a special ability: Stealth. The Stalker can turn invisible when it is immobile and has not fired any Bullets for about 2 seconds. While invisible, the player can still be damaged. When damaged, the tank is unveiled slightly, causing the tank to be visible. Should the Stalker move away, the invisibility cloak will completely drop. It is advised that as soon as an enemy notices you after getting hit by a bullet or polygon to move away or fire back immediately because even the tiniest contact will make you visible for a moment.

tables.heading: Overseer Upgrades
representative_rows:
colspan="4" |[[Overlord]]
Same as the Overseer, but now has four Spawners in which the Drones will spawn. The maximum of eight remains the same, but the Reload is essentially doubled. The core reload stat, however, does not change.

colspan="4" |[[Necromancer]]
The player now loses all ability to fire any sort of projectile. Instead, the player must “infect” a nearby Square using the tank’s body. That Square can infect other Squares, and so on until they can have a maximum army of up to 36 Squares (at Max [[Stats#Reload|Drone Count]]).
Reload turns into Drone Count, which increases max Drone Count by 2 per upgrade. These deadly Squares do less damage than the Overseer/Overlord’s Drones, but their vast number and sheer force can overwhelm opponents.

colspan="4" |[[Manager]]
The player now loses one Spawner, leaving only one remaining. This is mitigated somewhat since the sole Spawner produces Drones almost twice as fast, and eight Drones is still the cap. The Manager is also able to turn [[Invisibility|invisible]], similar to the Stalker and the Landmine.

colspan="4" |[[Overtrapper]]
The Overtrapper now has two controllable drones and two uncontrollable drones, and a trap placer in front. Despite having less drones than the Overseer. Also upgrades from Trapper

colspan="4" |[[Battleship]]
The Battleship replaces all of the player's Cannons with Mini Spawners that pump out s Drones at an extremely fast rate. Half the drones are manually controlled, and half are auto-controlled. However, Drones automatically disappear 4 seconds after spawning. These drones are also known as Partisans. Also upgrades from the Twin Flank.

tables.heading: Hunter Upgrades
representative_rows:
[[Predator]]
The Predator adds a third Cannon to the top of the tank and also gives it a unique ability where if the player holds right-click, they can focus their vision farther in the direction they are facing. The zoom screen doesn’t move with the player, though, so it is advised to zoom wisely! This tank is a combination of the old two-Cannon Predator and the [[X Hunter]]. Its Bullets have high damage stats. The distance of zoom is customizable. If the player clicks while the mouse pointer is way away, they will zoom a lot. If the pointer is close, they will not zoom as much.

[[Streamliner]]
The Streamliner replaces all Cannons with five short overlapping Cannons. They all fire one after another extremely quickly making for a pseudo-laser of Gunner Bullets. Also upgrades from Gunner.

tables.heading: Trapper Upgrades
representative_rows:
colspan="4" |[[Tri-Trapper]]
The Tri-Trapper has tripled Trap production, faster Reload, but shorter Trap lifespan. It is nearly a purely defensive tank and is best utilized to provide cover for teammates.

colspan="4" |[[Gunner Trapper]]
A unique combination of the Trapper and the Gunner. The two Cannons now point towards the player's mouse and the Launcher at the back now faces the opposite. It launches medium-sized Traps with the properties of regular ones. The Gunner Cannons have half the Reload but very high Penetration in return. Also upgrades from the Gunner.

colspan="4" |[[Overtrapper]]
It’s a Trapper with two AI Drones and two Manual Drones. This deadly combination can make this tank difficult to approach for non-snipers. Also upgrades from the Overseer.

colspan="4" |[[Mega Trapper]]
It makes the Launcher twice as large and makes it shoot Mega Traps, the second most powerful level 45 ammunition in the game. The Mega Trapper has lower Reload than the base Trapper, however, and shorter Trap lifespan.

colspan="4" |[[Auto Trapper]]
A Trapper with an uncontrolled Auto Turret on top. The Turret is powerful, has free rotation, and is deadly effective when combined with the defensive nature of the Trapper.

tables.heading: Destroyer Upgrades
representative_rows:
[[Hybrid]]
The Hybrid is a mix of the [[Overseer]] and the [[Destroyer]]. It has a Spawner at the back of the tank, with a maximum of two uncontrollable Drones. Then, of course, there’s the Destroyer Cannon.

[[Annihilator]]
Its [[Bullets|Bullet]] is larger than its predecessor's. It also has increased recoil and the same Reload. Its Bullet Damage is higher than the Destroyer’s.

[[Skimmer]]
A similar design to the Hunter but with wider Cannons, this tank has a [[Cannons|Deployer]] and shoots a Destroyer Bullet with two small cannons that are positioned 180 degrees apart. However, the main Bullet’s damage is significantly decreased. These bullets are known as [[missiles]]. As of now, only the Skimmer, the Rocketeer and the Glider use missiles.

[[Rocketeer]]
The Rocketeer fires bullets that have a [[Machine Gun]] [[Barrel]] on it's back, propelling the bullet forward with a slight inaccuracy due to the machine gun cannon’s nature. The Rocketeer missile is the most penetrating projectile in the game.

[[Glider]]
The Glider fires bullets that have two smaller [[Barrels]] on its back that are 35 degrees apart. This bullet used to be used by the [[Skimmer]].

tables.heading: Machine Gun Upgrades
representative_rows:
[[Sprayer]]
The Sprayer gains a secondary Cannon in the center of the large Cannon, which shoots Gunner Bullets at about half the Reload of the larger Cannon, albeit much more accurate. The Sprayer also has increased recoil and increased rate of fire when compared to the Machine Gun. It fires in a sequence of 3 Bullets where it shoots 1 normal-sized Bullet and then shoots another normal and 1 smaller Bullet simultaneously. The larger Bullet is as strong as a Machine Gun bullet, and the small one is seven times weaker. However, the big Cannon is wider and therefore less accurate, though the small cannon is not wide (and so, very accurate, just at the cost of doing significantly less Damage).

tables.heading: Smasher Upgrades
representative_rows:
colspan="2" |[[Landmine]]
A Smasher which can become [[Invisibility|invisible]] while not moving or taking damage for a full thirteen seconds. Due to the extended time required to become fully invisible, and the quickness with which it can be dispelled, it is strongly advised to use this tank with caution. The tank is made of two spinning hexagons, with one spinning half as fast.

colspan="2" |[[Auto Smasher]]
The controllable Auto Turret on top is the same as the Auto Gunner’s and the Auto Trapper’s, and this tank potentially deadly if enough points are spent on Bullet upgrades or [[Stats#Body Damage|body]] upgrades, but at the expense of either defense or an effective turret respectively. This tank is the only tank to have 10 upgrades for every stat.

colspan="2" |[[Spike]]
The [[Spike]] only increases [[Stats#Body Damage|Body Damage]]. It is the toughest tank in the game and will always defeat enemy rammers other than another spike. Its hull looks like 12 triangles evenly spaced out.

tables.heading: Special
representative_rows:
colspan="3" |[[Arena Closer]]
The Arena Closer is a tank that can only be used by a player in Sandbox Mode. The Closer only spawns in when a game is outdated or has been won by a team. The Arena Closers are much bulkier and faster than normal tanks and can one-shot any player.

colspan="3" |[[Mothership (Tank)|Mothership]]
The Mothership is a tank that exists in the Mothership and Sandbox game mode. In Mothership game mode, players must defend their team's mothership and capture the opposing team's Mothership. The Mothership game mode is back instead of Tag mode.

colspan="3" |[[Dominator]]
The Dominator is the only Tier 6 tank in the game, so it is special. However, it is only existent in the Domination game mode and cannot be obtained by upgrading; instead one will have to press H to control it.

colspan="3" |[[Ball|''"Ball"'']]
This nameless tank takes up the 53rd slot in the game's code. It is referred to as ID 53 or, more commonly, Ball. This tank is used as the default tank in the games code and is used in upgrade transitions and possessing [[Dominator]]s. At one point, this tank was used in the process of controlling [[Auto Turrets|Mounted Turrets]], but this feature no longer exists.

representative_rows:
[[Stalker]]
Originating from the Sniper branch, it upgrades from Assassin. By the time Diep.io was released, this was the most unique class. As it possessed sniper attributes, it could also turn invisible. Hence why it's named 'Stalker'. Its invisibility and range is why it became one of my favorite tanks.

[[Annihilator]]
Originating from the Machine Gun branch, it upgrades from Destroyer. Just look at this absolute unit. The most powerful class in the game, damage-wise. Unfortunately its movement and reload is slow. Although, it's satisfying when I one-shot some people with it.

{{2|Dual}}
A Twin-Sniper crossbranch, combining both Twin and Hunter. Basically just a better version of the Twin, but somewhat cooler. I think this because it's fun to imagine someone dualwielding handguns.

{{2|Falcon}}
A Flank-Sniper crossbranch, combining both Tri-Angle and Assassin. In my opinion, this tank is pretty trash but I like the design. It does kinda look like a bird.

{{2|Rifle}}
Upgrades from Sniper. I know it's worse than the Musket, but I prefer the Rifle because of its design. Just like the name says, it really does look like a rifle despite just using two shapes (excluding the base, of course). I mean, I like the Musket too.

tables.heading: Stages
representative_rows: You are sent to the sea bordering the Blue Team's land to destroy Rainbow's battleships, who plan to attack the Purple Team via water.
Unusually large amounts of trees are being cut down in Green Team territory, which poses a serious threat to both the local ecosystem and the world's climate. You are sent to investigate.
A large fleet of Rainbow aircraft are deployed from the hellish Yellow Desert to attack the Blue Team's cities. As maintainers of world peace, you must stop them before they reach their destination.
The normally hyper-aggressive Red Team armies have been silenced by an unknown force, and evidence points to Rainbow. You are again sent to stop them.

|775 tiles

tables.heading: List of Bosses
representative_rows: One of UraniumTactic's oldest creations, and arguably his ''oldest'' boss, Acrocity is an Elite Vanguard in Diep Z. He has 2 phases at the time being.
Acrocity is almost as old as Diep Z itself. He was created sometime around 2020.
Amber is a boss made for Diep Z. She can be found in the Dark Forest, normally residing in the Void City.
Amber's "scar" by her eye isn't a scar, but rather pure, exposed power. It glows when she is provoked to attack.
One of the many Elite Vanguards, Aniwe-Chan is a powerful Vanguard that can virtually instakill with her massive gatling guns, even able to destroy walls.
Aniwe has a confirmed redesign that hasn't been revealed yet.
Armed with massive turrets, missiles, armor, and shields, Arrowhead is nothing short of a terrifying enemy. She is the most common spawn for a Vanguard Raid.
Arrowhead actually had another form designed for Extended Arras, an existing collab.

|AI Entity
|Famous for having three other clones of him, Avalon is a Gauntlet boss and Trainer that can be found in the [[Fanon:The Arena|The Arena]] and [[Fanon:Diep Z- The Gauntlet|The Gauntlet]] as Ascension Avalon.
| -Passive (Normal)
-Hostile (Training and Gauntlet)
| -Wind Attacks
-Invisibility

|''No Image Available''

|Criospherians reside on the Criosphere, a massive space station. They rarely come down to the world of Diep Z, only travelling near for resources.
|Depends
|Criospherian defense shield
|Diep Z
|The Criosphere was always intended to be the largest entity, if not an entire planet. However, it was deemed to small to achieve that, so The Criosphere was adapted into the current version while Criospherians resemble the old one.
|-
|[[Fanon:Dart|Dart]]
|[[File:Dart.png|thumb]]
|Elite Vanguard
|The Vanguard Knight Dart is not a boss to be messed with. His armor isn't as strong as Arrowhead's, but he still has a bunch of swarm drones that he's not afraid to use.
|Hostile
| -Armor Effect
|Diep Z
|Dart and Arrowhead are siblings.
|-
|[[Defender]]
|[[File:Defender final icon2.png|thumb]]

|One of the bosses originating from the original Diep.io, the Defender is known for its powerful auto turrets and durable traps.
|Hostile
| -None
|Diep.io
|I couldn't decide if the Defender was a Polygon Boss or Nest Defender, and I almost said Polygon Boss but then considered what makes Polygon Bosses and Nest Defenders different? I know Nest Defenders are normally more advanced like Vanguards and Vis Ultima but-
|-
|[[Fanon:Diep Z- The Gauntlet|The Gauntlet]]
|[[File:Ascension Avalon.png|thumb|Ascension Avalon, the Wind Boss for the Gauntlet.]]
|Boss Rush
|With some of the finest elemental masters gathered, the Gauntlet is designed to be a training center for the tanks- only you'll actually have to fight.
|Hostile
| -Respective Elemental Powers
-Selectable stages
|Diep Z
|The Gauntlet Bosses are the only bosses that are naturally hostile to tanks below level 15. 
|-
|[[Guardian]]
|[[File:Guardian BOSS 1.png|thumb]]
|Polygon Boss
|What's more to say? It's a really big and strong crasher.
|Hostile
|N/A
|Diep.io
|The Guardian is technically the oldest boss to be put in Diep Z, being the first boss of the original game diep.io.
|-
|[[Fanon:Hard-Drive|Hard-Drive]]
|[[File:Hard Drive.png|thumb]]
|Elite Vanguard
|The Ultima Vanguard Superboss
|Hostile
|N/A
|Diep Z
|Not much currently known.
|-
|[[Fanon:Hycator|Hycator]]
|[[File:Hycator.png|thumb]]
|Dark Forest Secret Superboss
|Mysterious and fearsome, Hycator is one of the strongest residents of the Dark Forest. He resides in the Void of Ending.
| -Passive (normal)
-Hostile (if provoked)
| -Magic
-Transparency

-Flying/hovering
|Diep Z
|Hycator's eyes change color depending on his current state- red when angry, blue when passive. He also used to have a green laser. One more thing- he will jump out of the void to eat tanks below level 15. One could argue that this makes him hostile to tanks below 15, but he will only do so if they linger near the Void for too long. Plus, he one-shots them. Is that ''really'' hostile?
|-
|[[Fanon:Hystrigiel|Hystrigiel]]
|[[File:Hystrigiel.png|thumb]]
|Dark Forest Boss
|So enigmatic that not even Hycator knows much about him, Hystrigiel is a dagger-wielding Spectreum who scouts around the Dark Forest.
| -Neutral
| -Magic
-Phase Change

-Melee Daggers

-Flight

-Transparency
|Diep Z
|Hystrigiel is one of the many "oldies" of Diep Z, being designed for the older version.
|-
|[[Fanon:Infarion|Infarion]]
|[[File:Infarion.png|thumb]]
|Vis Class Boss
|Loaded with weapons, armor, and even working hands, Infarion is the largest boss in the entire world of Diep Z- which, by the way, has to grow just to allow him room to move!
| -Hostile
|Don't make me explain all of them...
|Diep Z
|Unlike most Vis-Class Bosses, Infarion's name doesn't start with "Vis" or end with an "A" (e.g. '''Vis''' Destructi'''a''', '''Vis''' Ultim'''a''', '''Vis''' Knighti'''a'''), making his base frame the only way to tell he's a Vis Boss. However, he wasn't always a Vis Boss- he had many iterations before this.
|-
|[[Fanon:Raid Bosses|Raid Bosses]]
|[[File:Marauder (Diep Z).png|thumb|A Marauder, a type of Raid Boss]]
|Raid Bosses
|No one asked for them, but we got them anyways. Ranging from fast to slow, deadly to nuisance, the raid bosses are large swarms of mini bosses who, namesakely so, love to raid tanks. 
|Hostile
| -Teampower
|Diep Z
|Most of the Raid Bosses were inspired by starblast.io ships.
|-
|[[Fanon:Raid-Master Vanguard|Raid-Master Vanguard]]
|[[File:Raid-Master Vanguard.png|thumb]]
|Undecided
|Leading raids of Vanguards, Raid Master Vanguards are dangerous leaders who give their friends the courage and strategy to fight any tank.
|Hostile
| -Teampower
-Influence Effect

-Armor Effect
|Diep Z
|The Raid Master Vanguard is obviously not a Normal or Elite Vanguard, but I can't decide if he should be a Modified or Special Vanguard.
|-
|[[Fanon:Raptor (Diep Z)|Raptor]]
|[[File:Raptor.png|thumb]]
|Dark Forest Vanguard Boss
|Swift and sneaky, this magic-possessing Vanguard hides in the Dark Forest, waiting for the opportune moment for an ambush.
| -Passive (stalking)
-Hostile
| -Invisibility
-Swiveling Arms

-Magic

-Can climb trees
|Diep Z
|Raptor accidentally hurt himself when practicing his magic, causing one of his eyes to permanently turn purple with his magic power.
|-
|[[Fanon:Smogdrid|Smogdrid]]
|[[File:Smogdrid Official.png|thumb]]
|Elite Vanguard Superboss
|It's a Vanguard! It's a mantis! It's a crab! It's a robot! It's... all four?! One of if not the first Elite Vanguard, Smogdrid has little to no projectile attacks, but with massive arms, high speed, and heavy armor, he'll be just fine with his two deadly claws.
|Very Hostile
| -Swivelling arms
-Opening/closing claws
| -Vanguards (original)
-Diep Z (current)
| -Smogdrid was originally modeled after a praying mantis, but his official/new design resembles a crab.
-Smogdrid is also technically the first Elite Vanguard, as his redesign was made before any of the other Elite Vanguards even existed (except for Acrocity, but he wasn't always an Elite Vanguard)
|-
|[[Fanon:Stealth (Diep Z)|Stealth]]
|[[File:Stealth.png|thumb]]
|Dark Forest Vanguard Boss
|Just as silent as her friend Raptor, Stealth sneaks around similar to Raptor, always preparing to attack any tanks who dare enter their territory.
| -Passive (stalking)
-Hostile
| -Invisibility
-Swiveling Arms

-Magic

-Can climb trees
|Diep Z
|It's not much of difference, but close observation can reveal that Stealth actually has slightly higher melee damage than Raptor. She's also a little faster.
|-
|[[Fanon:Ultima Fort|The Ultima Fort]]
|[[File:Ultima Fort.png|thumb]]
|Stationary Superboss
|(Technically) The largest boss in the game, with the [[Fanon:Criosphere (Diep Z)|Criosphere]] not being considered a boss (but still considered an entity). This behemoth is armed with trap launchers, turrets, and even spotlights to find enemies. It even harbors several bosses, making it difficult to fight this boss.
|Hostile
| -Spawns/harbors  Bosses
-Spotlights
-Power Core
|Diep Z
|The Ultima Fort has nothing to do with Vis Ultimas. In fact, Vis-Class bosses are one of two boss types that the Ultima Fort doesn't usually harbor, with the other being Septagon-class.
|-
|[[Fanon:The Uranium Tactician|The Uranium Tactician]]
|[[File:The Uranium Tactician (True Form).png|thumb]]
|''Unknown''
|Rumored to be the creator of Diep Z, the Uranium Tactician is a powerful boss. His first phase is so strong that almost no one has ever seen his true form.
| -Developer Controlled
-Hostile (Arena Closer)
| -Literally everything
| -Diep Z
-Vanguards

-UraniumTactics
| -It's rare, but Uranium Tactician doesn't need developer assistance to spawn- on rare occasions it will spawn as an Arena Closer.
-The Uranium Tactician can also be ranked under C, as he normally goes by Cavijesko.
|-
|[[Fanon:VAGNUARD|VAGNUARD]]
|[[File:VAGNAURD.png|thumb]]
|Elite Vanguard
|Unstable from glitching out too often, VAGNUARD is held steady by his strong mech suit. He normally only fires with his main auto turret and rocket launchers, but he can detach his side turrets to fire at enemies.
| -Hostile
| -Swiveling Robot Arms
-Missile Launchers

-Lasers

-Working Hands

|[[File:Vanguard_light.png|thumb]]

|One of the bosses not originating from Diep Z, the Vanguard is a Graviatar creation that was implemented into Diep Z.

tables.heading: Gamemodes
representative_rows: FFA, Stands for Free-For-All, is a gamemode with no teams, you color in ffa is blue and others in ffa is red.
This gamemode can shutdown in 5 hours or the player killed all players or there is no one playing.

Teams, You can be a colored team to help players if other teammates are attacking us, 2 Teams have Red and Blue, 4 Teams have Red, Green, Blue and Purple, 6 Teams have Red, Yellow, Green, Cyan, Blue and Purple.
This gamemode can shutdown if all your teammates destroyed all other teammates, you have 10 mins to left to play until the server shut downs.
Maze, Maze Teams and Maze Tag

Maze, Can be Maze Teams or Maze Tag, Maze will have some square walls around the map and, Maze Teams can be Maze 2 Teams or Maze 4 Teams, Just like these teams gamemodes expect 6 Teams will have a maze, Maze Tag has a square walls and a Tag mode.

This gamemode can shutdown in 5 hours (Maze FFA only) This gamemode can shutdown if all your teammates destroyed all other teammates, you have 10 mins to left to play until the server shut downs (Maze Teams only), This gamemode can shutdown if the teammate left killed other teammates or the map is fully shrinking. (Maze Tag only)
Tag is a gamemode that you can tag other players, Each are 6 colors: Red, Yellow, Green, Cyan, Blue and Purple, If you tagged all these the server will shutdown.
This gamemode can shutdown if the teammate left killed other teammates or the map is fully  shrinked.

representative_rows:
'''[[Fanon:Incendiary|Incendiary]]'''
The Incendiary fires bullets that deal less damage, but ignite the enemy for burn. Burn deals damage over time and can stack up to a limit.

'''[[Fanon:Airblast|Airblast]]'''
The Airblast fires bullets that deal minimal damage, but knock the enemy backwards. Knockback from behind the enemy, aimed towards the center, is only a quarter as effective to prevent major griefing. Knocking the same enemy back repeatedly has diminishing returns until it stops affecting it entirely.

'''[[Fanon:Grappler (Onett4smash)|Grappler]]'''
The Grappler fires a grappling hook with low damage, but drags whatever is attached towards the Grappler. While something is grabbed, the Grappler cannot move. Clicking again with something grabbed will release it.

'''[[Fanon:Charge Shot|Charge Shot]]'''
The Charge Shot can charge up bullets that have an increasing amount of damage and speed based on the charge duration; this is done by holding the fire button down, then releasing. Reload, however, is lengthened with a longer charge. Auto-Fire will have two modes: no charge and full charge.

tables.heading: The Stats.
representative_rows: ''Level 5 & below'': Max Health should be 2 or 3 points '''more''' than Body Damage
''Level 6'': Max Health should be 1, 2, or 3 points '''more''' than Body Damage
''Level 7–15'': Max Health should be 1 or 2 points '''more''' than Body Damage (unless maxed out)
''Level 16'': Max Health should be 1 or 2 points '''more''' or '''equal''' to Body Damage (unless maxed out)
''Level 17–25'': Max Health should be 1 point '''more''' or '''equal''' to Body Damage (unless maxed out)
